name: Zedekiah
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Then he made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's uncle, king in his stead and changed his name to Zedekiah; even a heathen king knew the throne had to stay in Solomon's line.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's father's brother, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Zedekiah was twenty one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and did evil in the sight of the Lord according to all Jehoiakim had done.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

points: The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: They slew his sons before his eyes, put out his eyes, and carried him bound to Babylon; Zedekiah was the last king of Judah, and his heirs were gone.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

note.label: 2 Kings 25: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Burning of the Temple

points: Josiah had four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum; Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah is the Jehoiachin of Kings and the Jechonias of Matthew.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: When the year is expired, Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon with the goodly vessels of the house of the Lord, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah of the priests in Anathoth, came in the days of Josiah, through Jehoiakim, and to the end of Zedekiah, up to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: Afterward He will deliver Zedekiah, his servants, and the people into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, to be smitten with the sword without pity or mercy.

note.label: Jeremiah 21: The Way of Life and the Way of Death

points: The evil figs are Zedekiah, his princes and those left in the land and in Egypt, delivered to be a reproach and a curse in every kingdom with sword, famine and pestilence. Good fig or bad fig is your decision.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

points: Like the evil figs that cannot be eaten, so the Most High will give up Zedekiah, his princes, and the residue of Jerusalem, including them that dwell in Egypt, to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth for their hurt.

note.label: Jeremiah 24: The Two Baskets of Figs

points: The Most High tells Jeremiah to make bonds and yokes, put them on his neck, and send them to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, and Zidon by their messengers to Zedekiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 27: The Yoke of Babylon

points: Jeremiah speaks the same words to Zedekiah, telling him to bring his neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him and live, rather than die by the sword, the famine, and the pestilence.

note.label: Jeremiah 27: The Yoke of Babylon

points: In the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, in the fifth month, Hananiah the son of Azur, a prophet of Gibeon, spake in the house of the Lord before the priests and all the people.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: Zedekiah had imprisoned him for prophesying that the Most High would give the city into the hand of the king of Babylon; Zedekiah himself would not escape but would be led to Babylon, speak with him mouth to mouth, and behold his eyes.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

points: Zedekiah made a covenant to free every Hebrew servant, and then they took them back into subjection.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

points: King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: After Jeremiah has remained many days in the dungeon and its cells, Zedekiah secretly sends for him and asks if there is any word from the Most High; Jeremiah answers there is, that the king shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: He pleads not to be sent back to the house of Jonathan the scribe lest he die there; Zedekiah commands he be kept in the court of the prison and given a daily piece of bread out of the bakers' street until all the bread in the city is spent.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: In the ninth year of Zedekiah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar and all his army come against Jerusalem and besiege it, and in the eleventh year, the fourth month, the ninth day, the city is broken up.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: The princes of the king of Babylon come in and sit in the middle gate; when Zedekiah and the men of war see them, they flee by night by the way of the king's garden through the gate between the two walls toward the plain.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: The Chaldean army pursues and overtakes Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where the king of Babylon slays Zedekiah's sons and all the nobles of Judah before his eyes, then puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him with chains for Babylon, and burns the king's house and the houses of the people, breaking down the walls of Jerusalem.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: This word came against Elam in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah. Elam is the ancient and modern Persians, the so-called East Indians found in India, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, and Iran.

note.label: Jeremiah 49: Judgment on Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar, and Elam

points: Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever.

note.label: Jeremiah 51: The Full Recompense of Babylon

points: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
Zedekiah was not of the royal lineage per se, and Zedekiah was not really his name; to see how he became king we go back to when Babylon took the real king away.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: He did that which was evil in the eyes of the Most High as Jehoiakim had done, and through the anger of the Most High against Jerusalem and Judah, Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.
The Most High had told through Jeremiah that the people would have to serve Babylon seventy years, but Zedekiah decided to rebel against it instead of submitting to the prophecy.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: They brought Zedekiah to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where he gave judgment upon him, and the king of Babylon slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes and slew all the princes of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

points: Then they put out Zedekiah's eyes, so the last thing he would ever see was his sons put to death in his face, and they bound him in chains, carried him to Babylon, and kept him in prison till the day of his death; the Most High allowed these heathen to bring hell into Jerusalem.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

cases.name: Zedekiah
cases.charge: Doing evil in the sight of the Lord; humbling not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord; rebelling against Nebuchadnezzar who had made him swear by God; stiffening his neck and hardening his heart from turning unto the Lord God of Israel
cases.preview: Nebuchadnezzar made Mattaniah king as Zedekiah and bound him by an oath sworn by God;
